knowledge:
- key_parameters: <read1=Path to the input FASTQ file (or vector of paths) for read 1 ;; read2=Path to the input FASTQ file (or vector of paths) for read 2 ;; outputFastq=Prefix or path for the output trimmed FASTQ file(s) ;; thread=Number of threads to use for multi-threading ;; merge=Logical; if TRUE, merges paired-end reads after QC ;; mergeOut=Path for the merged output FASTQ file when merge=TRUE ;; umi=Logical; enables UMI (Unique Molecular Identifier) preprocessing ;; umiLoc=Location of UMI (e.g., "read1", "read2") ;; umiLength=Length of the UMI sequence ;; disableTrimPolyG=Logical; disables polyG trimming (often needed for NextSeq/NovaSeq data) ;; cutLowQualFront=Logical; enables trimming of low-quality bases from the 5' end ;; cutLowQualTail=Logical; enables trimming of low-quality bases from the 3' end ;; adapterSequenceRead1=Custom adapter sequence to trim from read 1>
- alternatives: <None mentioned in the documentation; the package serves as the direct R interface to the C++ command-line tool fastp.>
- when_to_use: <Use when preprocessing raw single-end or paired-end FASTQ sequencing data to perform quality control, adapter trimming, low-quality base filtering, or UMI extraction before downstream alignment or analysis.>
- pitfalls: <Ensure correct UMI parameters (umiLoc, umiLength) are set to avoid misidentifying or losing UMI sequences. Note that curvePlot() may trigger a deprecation warning due to internal use of aes_string() in older ggplot2 versions, though it still functions correctly.>

workflows.name: single_end_qc_trimming
workflows.intent: Perform quality control, adapter trimming, and quality filtering on single-end FASTQ data, followed by generating summary tables and plots.
workflows.stages: 1. Run rfastp on the single-end FASTQ file ;; 2. Generate base quality and GC content plots ;; 3. Extract summary statistics.
workflows.code:
se_read1 <- system.file("extdata","Fox3_Std_small.fq.gz",package="Rfastp")
outputPrefix <- tempfile(tmpdir = tempdir())
se_json_report <- rfastp(read1 = se_read1, 
    outputFastq = paste0(outputPrefix, "_se"), thread = 4)
p1 <- curvePlot(se_json_report)
p1
p2 <- curvePlot(se_json_report, curve="content_curves")
p2

workflows.name: paired_end_qc_trimming_merging
workflows.intent: Perform quality control, adapter trimming, and optional merging on paired-end FASTQ data, followed by extracting summary statistics.
workflows.stages: 1. Run rfastp on paired-end FASTQ files ;; 2. Run rfastp with read merging enabled ;; 3. Extract QC and trimming summaries.
workflows.code:
pe_read1 <- system.file("extdata","reads1.fastq.gz",package="Rfastp")
pe_read2 <- system.file("extdata","reads2.fastq.gz",package="Rfastp")
outputPrefix <- tempfile(tmpdir = tempdir())
pe_json_report <- rfastp(read1 = pe_read1, read2 = pe_read2,
    outputFastq = paste0(outputPrefix, "_pe"))
pe_merge_json_report <- rfastp(read1 = pe_read1, read2 = pe_read2, merge = TRUE,
    outputFastq = paste0(outputPrefix, '_unpaired'),
    mergeOut = paste0(outputPrefix, "_merged.fastq.gz"))
dfsummary <- qcSummary(pe_json_report)
dfTrim <- trimSummary(pe_json_report)

workflows.name: umi_processing
workflows.intent: Preprocess paired-end FASTQ files containing Unique Molecular Identifiers (UMIs), extracting and appending them to read headers.
workflows.stages: 1. Run rfastp with standard UMI extraction parameters ;; 2. Run rfastp with customized UMI prefix and location parameters.
workflows.code:
pe_read1 <- system.file("extdata","reads1.fastq.gz",package="Rfastp")
pe_read2 <- system.file("extdata","reads2.fastq.gz",package="Rfastp")
outputPrefix <- tempfile(tmpdir = tempdir())
umi_json_report <- rfastp(read1 = pe_read1, read2 = pe_read2, 
    outputFastq = paste0(outputPrefix, '_umi1'), umi = TRUE, umiLoc = "read1",
    umiLength = 16)
umi_json_report <- rfastp(read1 = pe_read1, read2 = pe_read2, 
    outputFastq = paste0(outputPrefix, '_umi2'), umi = TRUE, umiLoc = "read1",
    umiLength = 16, umiPrefix = "#", umiNoConnection = TRUE, 
    umiIgnoreSeqNameSpace = TRUE)

workflows.name: concatenate_fastq_files
workflows.intent: Concatenate multiple split FASTQ files into a single output FASTQ file.
input: splited_001_R2.fastq.gz, splited_002_R2.fastq.gz, splited_003_R2.fastq.gz, splited_004_R2.fastq.gz (Split FASTQ files)
workflows.stages: 1. Define a vector of input file paths ;; 2. Concatenate files using catfastq.
